correctness.rationale: A transitive symmetric rank-three action has commutative permutation commutant span{I,B,11*}, implying multiplicity-free decomposition 1⊕V_θ⊕V_τ and one-dimensional H-fixed line in each irreducible block. For f=1_{A_J}, coset averaging gives each nontrivial Fourier coefficient as a rank-one block with singular value determined by the sum of spherical orbit vectors. After normalizing the induced vectors, the nontrivial trace-norm terms are sqrt[(d_θ/n)(1_J*P_θ1_J)] and sqrt[(d_τ/n)(1_J*P_τ1_J)]. With P_θ=[B−τI−(k−τ)P0]/(θ−τ), P_τ=[θI−B+(k−θ)P0]/(θ−τ), 1_J*B1_J=2e, P0=11*/n, the displayed q_θ,q_τ follow; q≥0 as projector squared norms. Scalar Fourier block r/n completes the formula. Independently checked boundary J empty, singleton, full for the Johnson(4,2) rank-three example, giving norms 0,1,1; actual S4 verifier code inspected but its stored log not regarded as independent proof. The theorem requires symmetric (undirected orbitals) rank three.
residual_risks: The conclusion depends on self-paired orbitals and exactly two nontrivial constituents; noncommutative/nonsymmetric rank-three actions are outside the claim.

value.rationale: For each finite symmetric rank-three permutation action and every union of point-stabilizer cosets, the full noncommutative Fourier-algebra nuclear norm collapses to two elementary combinatorial statistics: number of selected vertices and induced orbital edges. The structural identity naturally links strongly regular graph geometry and Fourier idempotent norms, provides exact nontrivial benchmarks beyond the triangle bound, and holds for an infinite family of finite groups/sets rather than a tiny case.
